question.text: A 'side pocket' provision in an AIF's fund documents is BEST described as:

answer.text: A fee-sharing arrangement between placement agents
A mechanism to segregate illiquid or distressed investments into a separate accounting compartment, so valuation / redemption issues do not contaminate the main portfolio
A type of co-investment opportunity offered to anchor LPs
A regulatory reserve required under SEBI (AIF) Regulations at 5% of corpus

explanation.text: The Logic: A side pocket is a portfolio-accounting tool that segregates illiquid or distressed positions into a separate compartment, so valuation uncertainty and redemption issues on those holdings do not contaminate the main "clean" portfolio. LPs continue to subscribe/redeem against the main portfolio at a meaningful NAV, while the side-pocketed positions are realised over time and proceeds distributed to investors who were holders at the date of side-pocketing. The Trap: A placement-agent fee-share (A) is an unrelated economic arrangement. A co-investment opportunity (C) is a structural offer to anchor LPs, not a portfolio-segregation mechanism. A 5%-of-corpus regulatory reserve (D) is a fabricated rule — SEBI (AIF) Regulations do not impose any such reserve. Note: The specific concept of side pockets as a mechanism to segregate illiquid/distressed investments is not explicitly described in the cited workbook chapter (FINAL_Series-XIX-C_AIF Managers_Ver-Dec-2025.pdf, pp. 124, 441, 494), which discusses green shoe, secondaries valuation, and close-ended redemption restrictions. The framing above is general industry knowledge of side-pocket mechanics in alternative funds.
